questions.stem: A reviewer is weighing competing claims about a stop condition written as a purpose, among them "Ignore signal". Based only on the excerpt above, which answer is the one the evidence warrants?
questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: close reading of the note yields this rule: the beep is the stopping point. On that basis "Stop when signal beeps" is the supported choice. Option A ("Continue after beep") fails because it reads until as forever; Option C ("Stop before beep") fails because it reverses trigger and action; Option D ("Ignore signal") fails because it drops stated purpose.

questions.topic: The line that says nothing can be done

stimulus.body: A short reference note on the line that says nothing can be done is set for a close-reading task. It states: The no-review line closes the matter. A marginal reminder adds: accept final notice. Four statements are then offered, and only one of them follows from what the note actually says.

questions.stem: The passage above presents a case and the terms needed to judge it. Based only on what the passage establishes about the line that says nothing can be done, which choice holds up?

answer.exemplar: A notice stating no further review is available must be accepted, and the matter closed rather than reopened through repeated requests.

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: the no-review line closes the matter. On that basis "A notice stating no further review is available must be accepted, and the matter closed rather…" is the supported choice.

questions.topic: Overlapping instructions in two sections

stimulus.body: The working note below records the evidence for a claim about overlapping instructions in two sections. conflicting safety guidance must be reconciled first. A marginal reminder adds: reconcile first. A reader must decide which of the four proposed statements the note warrants, without using outside knowledge.

questions.stem: Read the excerpt above and decide what it establishes about overlapping instructions in two sections. Does it support the claim "Follow section two", or must a different option be chosen?
questions.explanation: What settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: what settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: conflicting safety guidance must be reconciled first. On that basis "Reconcile before acting" is the supported choice. Option A ("Follow section one") fails because it first section always wins; Option B ("Follow section two") fails because it later section always wins; Option C ("Skip the guard") fails because it avoids required work.
